list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.18
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.18
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The Spotify sign-in window captures the cookies now, and that is what made the import look broken.** The cookie walk returns nothing usable because of one return value: in JCEF `CefCookieVisitor.visit` returns *keep visiting*, and the window returned `false`, which ends the walk after the very first cookie. That first cookie is almost never `sp_dc`, so every capture came back empty and the screen stayed on "Not connected to Spotify" while the sign-in itself had worked - exactly what the report said, and what `spotify.log` showed (the pages loaded, no `captured sp_dc` line ever followed). **Verified on JCEF 152.0.6 with a standalone probe against the same CEF build:** with `false` a visit of a five-cookie store delivers one cookie (`count=0 total=5`, then nothing); with `true` it delivers all five in milliseconds and deletes none. **Also verified there:** the visit must NOT be submitted from the AWT event thread - CEF dispatches the visitor callbacks on that same thread, so an event-thread visit waited three seconds and delivered zero callbacks, which is why the walk stays on the window's own thread. **Watch:** with the blocked-Google message gone the sign-in must also end by itself: `spotify.log` has to show `JCEF cookie visit returned N cookie(s): …` and then `JCEF sign-in captured sp_dc`.
- [DE] **The sign-in window no longer claims Google blocked it while the user is typing on Spotify's own form.** `onAddressChange` fires for every frame, and Spotify's sign-in page embeds Google's script, whose `accounts.google.com` iframe was enough to replace the status line and reveal *Retry* and *Open it in your browser* over a page that was working. Only the main frame is read now.
- [DE] **A language in place of another: two Developer options rows were labelled with a raw setting name.** `detailed_playback_logging` and `detailed_startup_logs` hold the literal text `DetailedPlaybackLogging` and `DetailedStartupLogs` in **all 52 languages**, so those two switches were introduced by an identifier no user should ever read. The rows show the description that was already translated everywhere. **Watch:** the audit's new cross-language checks (below) must stay clean.
- [DE] **The JVM heap actually changes now, and the app says so.** Choosing a size looked like a no-op for two reasons. The restart never happened: the code looked for a `java` launcher inside the bundled runtime, and a jpackage image does not ship one (`runtime/bin` on the installed 1.54.17 image has `java.dll` and no `java.exe`), so it gave up silently; the launcher's own `.cfg`, which holds `-Xmx2g`, sits under `Program Files` and cannot be rewritten either. What the launcher does honour is `_JAVA_OPTIONS`, and it is applied after the `.cfg`, so it replaces that `-Xmx`. **Verified against the installed image before writing this:** `VIVIMusic.exe` started with `_JAVA_OPTIONS=-Xmx3072m` came up with a maximum heap of 3221225472 bytes instead of the image's 2 GB. The restart is also watched now - if the new process exits at once, the app stays up and `app.log` records the exit code - and every decision is logged (`jvm heap: …`), so a heap that does not take effect can no longer be a silent no-op. **Verified:** the same probe on the installed runtime confirms the image's classpath resolves `com.music.vivi.desktop.MainKt`. **Constraint:** a launch from the Start Menu has no variable set, so it comes up on the image's 2 GB and the app corrects itself a moment later through the same path; that is also what makes a size chosen while the app was closed take effect.

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The translation audit also looks for a language standing in another language's place.** Three checks were added to `scripts/audit_desktop_localization.py`: the language code must be served by its own table (`"zh-rCN"` by `strings_zh_rCN`, not by a neighbour's), the picker must name each code with that language's own endonym ("Polski" for `pl`), and a value may not carry a letter that belongs to another language's alphabet (`ß`, `ł`, `ő`, `đ`, `õ`, `ñ` and the rest, with the letters several languages share kept out of the comparison so a language is never reported against its own text). **Result on this tree:** 52 languages, 822 English keys, 0 missing or leaking, 0 wrong-script, 0 foreign letters, and the two raw identifiers above found and fixed. The three remaining `English text left` entries are `jvm_memory_default` in Filipino, Indonesian and `in`, where "Default" is the local word.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The heap preparation bar moved to the screen that opened the sign-in window.** It used to sit in the window's own header, next to the status and the ways out, which is not where the user is looking when a first run spends a while downloading and unpacking Chromium. It is now drawn under **Sign in to Spotify** on the import screen, with the percentage, and it is not shown at all once the page is up.
- [DE] **The sign-in window's header is one row again:** a spinner and the status, with *Retry* and *Open it in your browser* appearing in that same row only after Google refuses its page. Both are flat, borderless and in the accent the other sign-in window's links use, so the two windows read as the same program; the long blocked sentence is carried in full in the row's tooltip instead of being clipped.
- [DE] **Turn off developer options is a switch now**, the way Android's own developer-options screen turns them off, instead of a row that opens a question. It sits first and still asks once, because turning it off resets every option below.
- [DE] **The account row at the bottom left opens the Account screen directly.** The row *is* the account (name and avatar), so landing on the general settings list meant clicking the same thing twice; the gear in the rail is the way to that list. The row stays highlighted on both screens.
- [DE] **The expressive player's panel can no longer be closed by accident.** The queue / lyrics / history tabs used to toggle the panel off, and they took the tab strip down with them: once the panel was closed there was no control left to open it again, so the only way back was to relaunch the app. The tabs are selectors now, the panel and its strip are always there, and the stored tab is restored on the section the user left it on (a stored "closed" from an older build opens on the queue). The player itself still closes with the chevron at the top left.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.18: capture the Spotify cookies, and make the JVM heap change

---
This release was built automatically from commit `2dab3978cc1a785c73fc9d57108f790136520fa8`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.17
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.17
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The main window remembers its size and position again.** The placement was saved correctly (`1207x1017@621,58` in `settings.json`) but the restore clamped it into the rectangle `maximumWindowBounds` reports before the window is shown, and that rectangle came back bogus (`526x478@621,597`): the clamp then both shrank and moved a perfectly valid placement, and every logged session opened at exactly that size. The saved floating bounds are clamped only against a screen the environment reports as *real* (at least 800x600) now; a bogus or smaller one is ignored and the saved size is used as it is. The restore is also re-asserted once the window is actually shown, and the decision is logged (`restore: saved=… usable=… applied=…` in `window.log`) so the next session shows exactly what was applied.
- [DE] **Quitting from the tray keeps the window's placement too.** The tray's Quit called `exitApplication` directly and never ran the close request that persists the geometry, so a session ended from the tray reopened at the previous size and position. Both exit paths persist it now, and a minimized window's parked bounds (`-32000,-32000 160x28`) are no longer written, which would otherwise be restored as the window's placement.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.17: restore the main window's saved size and position

---
This release was built automatically from commit `6897ccd17957a165e16298f28a5b08f193d5c88c`.

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.16
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.16
**Release channel:** `beta`

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The Spotify sign-in window remembers its size and shows what it is doing.** Its size and position are saved on close and restored on the next opening (`spotifyLoginWindowWidth/Height/X/Y` in `settings.json`), for the JCEF window and the JavaFX fallback alike, and a progress bar sits in its header: it carries the real jcefmaven download/extract percentage while the CEF natives are prepared (about 100 MB on the first try, which used to look like a hang) and turns into an indeterminate bar while a page loads.

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The Retry and Open it in your browser buttons are no longer clipped.** The status line was a single-line label, and the long "Google blocked" sentence pushed the two buttons out of the header, where they came out cut in half and unusable. The status wraps over two lines now and the buttons live on their own row under it, so neither can be swallowed by the text.
- [DE] **The JCEF sign-in can actually complete.** CEF delivers a cookie visit asynchronously on its own thread, and the capture read the store after the call had already returned, so it almost always saw nothing and the window never closed itself. Each visit is awaited now (bounded), the scoped visit is backed by a full-store one filtered to `spotify.com`, every finished page load is logged (`JCEF page loaded (…)`) so a window that does not capture can be told from one that never loaded, and a CEF that cannot start falls back to the JavaFX window in the same attempt instead of on the user's next press.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.16: take the JCEF window down when the browser cannot attach
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.16: sign-in window size memory, progress and a working JCEF capture

---

list.name: Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.15
list.body:
## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.15
**Release channel:** `beta`

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The Spotify sign-in window is a real Chromium now (JCEF).** The embedded window that gets the `sp_dc` cookie opened a JavaFX `WebEngine`, and Google refuses its own sign-in page inside an engine it recognises as embedded (`disallowed_useragent`, issue #97). The window is backed by JCEF (a complete Chromium Embedded Framework) now, so the page sees the Chromium engine rather than a WebView that claims to be Chrome: it announces a per-OS desktop Chrome user agent and captures `sp_dc` / `sp_key` off CEF's own cookie store, scoped to `https://open.spotify.com`, the same way the old window did off `java.net.CookieManager`. The JavaFX window stays as the fallback for a machine where CEF cannot start. **Constraint:** the CEF natives are about 100 MB and jcefmaven downloads and unpacks them under `~/.vivimusic/cef` the first time the window is opened, so the packaged installers keep their size and the first sign-in is slower. **Unverified in this environment:** whether Chromium passes Google's check where the `WebEngine` did not; no GUI and no account are available here, so the first real attempt has to confirm the sign-in page loads; the blocked-page message and the **Open it in your browser** link stay for the case where Google still refuses.

### 🔧 Changed
- [DE] **The Debug & Developer Options screen turned off the Android way.** **Turn off developer options** is the first row of the screen now (it used to be the last), and turning it off resets everything the screen exposes in the same step: the JVM heap goes back to the launcher default, both verbose-log switches go off and the APK-download button is hidden again, next to the `developerUnlocked` flag the seven-tap sets. Before, only the flag was cleared and the options kept whatever the user had chosen.

### 🐛 Fixed
- [DE] **The changelog is no longer letter-spaced.** The bundled emoji font's character map also lists some ordinary ASCII (`U+0020` the space, `U+0023` `#`, `U+002A` `*` and the digits, which are the keycap bases), and the renderer routed every one of those codepoints to that font because it only asked "does the font have this glyph". Inside the emoji font's wide cell they came out spaced: every digit of a version (`1 . 5 4 . 1 1`), every `#97` and, through the space, every word gap in the body read as if it had been tracked out. Everything below `U+00A9` is the app font's business and no longer goes near an emoji fallback.
- [DE] **The changelog's section-heading emoji are drawn, not blank.** 1.54.13 added a custom colour subset of Noto Color Emoji and routed the emoji codepoints to it, but Skiko does not paint its COLR/CPAL glyphs: `✨ Added` lost its mark entirely and `🔧 Changed` / `🐛 Fixed` fell back to a notdef diamond. The colour family is not used any more (its codepoints go to the monochrome Noto Emoji, which Skia always draws), and the font and its coverage stay bundled so the branch can be switched back once a renderer paints COLR.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.15: wait for the JCEF cookie visit before reading the capture
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.15: JCEF sign-in window, changelog spacing and emoji, dev-options reset
- docs: keep the browser sign-in link and do not embed JCEF

---
This release was built automatically from commit `481884466d46f39181ad03f51e29ff1a78d86167`.

## Vivi Music 6.0.8.5_DE 1.54.14
**Release channel:** `beta`

### ✨ Added
- [DE] **The Developer options screen is now "Debug & Developer Options", and it can turn itself off again.** The screen carries the new name in all 53 languages, and a new row at its end, **Turn off developer options**, hides it and locks it again exactly like Android's own system developer options: a short confirmation says what will happen, then the unlock flag the seven-tap sets is cleared, so System > Advanced disappears and the seven-tap on the About version code is the only way back. The four new keys (`debug_developer_options`, `disable_developer_options`, `disable_developer_options_desc`, `disable_developer_options_confirm`) are translated in every language, so the localization audit stays clean.

### 📝 Commits
- v6.0.8.5_DE-1.54.14: Debug & Developer Options rename, turn-off row
